question: Can I build up unused FHSA participation room in years before I open my first FHSA?
generated_answer:
Yes, you can build up unused FHSA participation room in years before you open your first FHSA. This is because the 10% limit on FHSA contributions applies to each year's contributions, not to the total amount you can contribute over your lifetime. So, if you don't use all of your FHSA room in a given year, you can carry it forward to future years. This means that if you don't open your first FHSA until, say, age 30, you could potentially contribute up to 10% of your income for each of the previous 20 years (from age 10 to 29), as long as you have not already used up that room in previous years.

For example, if you earn $50,000 at age 30 and open your first FHSA, you could contribute up to $5,000 (10% of $50,000) to your FHSA that year. However, if you had earned $50,000 each year from age 10 to 29 and had not used any of your FHSA room in those years, you could potentially contribute up to $50,000 x 20 years = $100,000 to your FHSA at age 30, as long as you have not already used up that room in previous years.

It's important to note that while you can carry forward unused FHSA room, there is a lifetime limit of $40,000 on total FHSA contributions. So, even if you have built up a lot of unused room, you cannot contribute more than $40,000 in total to your FHSA over your lifetime.

Also, keep in mind that if you do not use your FHSA room in a given year, you will not be able to carry it forward to future years if you do not open an FHSA. So, if you want to build up unused FHSA room, you need to open an FHSA and make contributions to it in each year that you have room available.

Overall, building up unused FHSA room in years before you open your first FHSA can be a good strategy if you expect to have a high income in future years and want to take advantage of the tax benefits of the FHSA. However, it's important to carefully consider your individual circumstances and to consult with a financial advisor to determine the best approach for you.
